perf: Van Gogh painted this skeleton smoking, as a *joke.*
In 1886, he was an art student in Antwerp.
Students drew skeletons, but nobody painted one.
In nine months, he ate maybe six or seven hot meals.
He smoked a lot, so he'd feel less *hungry.*
His teeth were breaking off, one after another.
A joke about death, or about *himself?*

cover.question: Why is this skeleton smoking?
cover.name: VINCENT VAN GOGH
cover.work: Head of a Skeleton with a Burning Cigarette, 1886
cover.answered_by: A student's joke in Antwerp (skeletons were drawn at the academy, never painted), made while he was starving, smoking to dull his hunger and losing his teeth

facts.claim: Van Gogh painted the skeleton with a lit cigarette as a (juvenile) joke; the Van Gogh Museum dates it January–February 1886
He painted it in early 1886 while studying at the art academy in Antwerp (Royal Academy of Fine Arts)
Drawing skeletons was a standard exercise at the academy, but painting them was not part of the curriculum
Letter to Theo, Antwerp, c. 3-4 February 1886: since moving into his own studio on 1 May (1885) he had 'not had a hot dinner more than perhaps six or seven times since'
Same letter: he had made it worse 'by smoking a great deal, which I did the more because then one does not feel an empty stomach so much'
Same letter: 'more and more of my teeth broke off' (vangoghletters.org: teeth breaking off one after another); he paid a dentist 50 francs

Wikipedia: likely meant as a kind of joke, probably also a comment on conservative academic practice; interpretations differ (a joke born of boredom, or death treated with humour); painted when van Gogh was in poor health. The narration leaves the question open
Van Gogh was a keen smoker and continued to smoke until his death in 1890
The painting belongs to the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam (Vincent van Gogh Foundation)

caption:
Van Gogh painted this skeleton smoking, as a joke.

In January and February 1886 he was a student at the art academy in Antwerp. Drawing skeletons was a standard exercise there, to learn anatomy; painting them was not part of the lessons. So, somewhere between classes, he gave this one a lit cigarette.

The joke has a darker side. In a letter to his brother Theo that February, Vincent wrote that since the previous May he had not had a hot dinner more than perhaps six or seven times. He had been "smoking a great deal", because then you don't feel an empty stomach so much, and more and more of his teeth were breaking off. A doctor told him he absolutely must take better care of himself.

A few weeks later he left Antwerp for Paris. He kept smoking until his death in 1890.

It hangs in the Van Gogh Museum, in Amsterdam.

👁️ A joke about death, or about himself?
caption_short: Van Gogh painted this skeleton smoking, as a joke. But he was the one smoking to forget his hunger. 👁️
